prompt:
Write 6 short claim log entries (one to three sentences each) by an auto insurance adjuster for a rear-end collision claim, in time order. Injury: neck strain. The claimant is represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1481; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- It is not yet clear whether the injury came from this crash.
- Treatment followed a usual course and tapered off as the patient improved.
- No earlier injury to the same body area is known.
- Witnesses, photos and the other driver all confirm the accident happened as described.
- The vehicle damage matches the described impact.
- The claimant told the same account in every conversation.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- Nothing suggests the damage happened before the coverage started.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text:
Entry 1: Claim opened after the insured reported being rear-ended at a traffic signal. The claimant, who is represented by counsel, has been identified as a passenger in the vehicle, and the police report and two independent witnesses place her in the car at the time of impact.

Entry 2: Photos from the scene and the other driver's statement both match the described impact, and the damage pattern on the rear bumper and trunk lines up with what the witnesses describe. Nothing in the file suggests any damage existed before the policy period began, and the driver is named on the policy.

Entry 3: Counsel's letter describes neck pain following the collision. The claimant's account of how the crash happened has been the same in every conversation so far, and no earlier injury to the neck or upper back is known from prior records requested to date.

Entry 4: Medical records received show a usual course of treatment, including physical therapy and a short course of medication, with symptoms easing steadily as the claimant improved. It is still not clear whether the injury came from this crash or from another cause, and an independent review has been requested.

Entry 5: No earlier damage to the claimant's vehicle is known from the prior claims search or from the owner's records. The repair estimate is being reviewed against the photos and the impact description.

Entry 6: Treatment has tapered off and the claimant's most recent visit notes improvement. Causation remains open pending the independent review, and the file is being kept active until the review and counsel's demand are received.
